subject: Media Literacy
title: Cave Paintings: The First Media
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cave Paintings: The First Media.

hook.text: 40,000 years ago, someone pressed a hand against a cave wall and blew pigment around it.

buildup.text: Cave paintings in Lascaux and Altamira were humanity's first attempt to record and share ideas.

discovery.text: These weren't random doodles. They depicted hunts, animals, and rituals — they told stories.

twist.text: Some caves show the same images repainted over centuries — early media was already being updated.

climax.text: Before language was written, humans found a way to make their stories outlast their voices.

punchline.text: The first media was a handprint on stone.

quiz.question: What was the purpose of early cave paintings?
options: Recording and sharing stories and ideas
